Outcome-Null Calibration Check for STABL

Source: R/null_validation.R
stabl_null_check.Rd

Repeatedly reruns the complete stabl_fit() pipeline on outcome-null versions of the data (permuted or explicitly simulated) and summarizes null selection behavior: the selected-panel-size distribution, the probability of selecting anything at all, per-feature selection frequencies, reported-FDP+ versus by-construction realized FDP, and null-saturation proportions.

Usage

stabl_null_check(
  x,
  y,
  design = c("independent", "within_block", "whole_cluster", "simulated"),
  fit_spec = list(),
  n_reps = 20L,
  blocks = NULL,
  clusters = NULL,
  null_simulator = NULL,
  decoy_reps = 1L,
  seed = NULL,
  max_failures = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Numeric predictor matrix with non-empty row names (sample ids) and column names (feature ids), as for stabl_fit().

y

Outcome vector, named to match rownames(x).

design

Exchangeability unit prescribing the null: one of "independent" (global permutation; refused when blocks or clusters are supplied), "within_block" (permute within blocks), "whole_cluster" (permute whole cluster outcome vectors across clusters), or "simulated" (use null_simulator).

fit_spec

Named list of further arguments for stabl_fit(), e.g. list(n_bootstraps = 50, artificial_type = "knockoff_equi"). The per-replicate random_state is always set by stabl_null_check; lambda_grid defaults to "auto" when not supplied.

n_reps

Number of null replicates (permutations or simulated nulls). Total fits = n_reps * decoy_reps.

blocks

Optional factor/vector of length nrow(x) giving block membership; required for design = "within_block".

clusters

Optional factor/vector of length nrow(x) giving cluster membership; required for design = "whole_cluster".

null_simulator

Required for design = "simulated": a function function(y, x, rep_id, seed) returning a null outcome vector (named like y). Under this design the truth is synthetic: every selected feature is a false positive by construction.

decoy_reps

Number of fit replicates per null replicate with distinct decoy-generator seeds; values > 1 separate sensitivity to the random decoy realization from sensitivity to the null permutation.

seed

Optional base seed. Per-replicate permutation and fit seeds are derived from it by the package's hashed multi-stream derivation and stored in the result, so any replicate is exactly replayable. If NULL, a seed is drawn from the current RNG state and recorded.

max_failures

Bound on tolerated fit failures. Every failure is recorded with its replicate id, seeds, and error message; if failures exceed max_failures the run aborts (fail-closed) rather than summarizing a mostly-failed design.

...

Reserved; unused arguments are an error.

Value

A stabl_null_validation object with elements:

design, truth_status

The exchangeability unit and whether the null truth is "synthetic_global_null" (design "simulated") or "induced_global_null_permutation" (permutation designs).

n_reps, decoy_reps, n_failures, failures

Replication counts and a data frame of bounded failure records.

replicates

Per-replicate results: seeds, panel size, selected features, reported FDP+ minimum and threshold, at-selection real/artificial proportions, and decoy-generator provenance.

panel_sizes

Integer vector of selected-panel sizes.

p_any_selection

Probability the null pipeline selects at least one feature.

feature_frequency

Named, decreasing vector of per-feature null selection frequencies.

reported_fdp_plus

Reported FDP+ minima across replicates; under the global null the realized FDP is 1 whenever the panel is non-empty, by construction.

fit_spec, call

The executed fit specification and call.

Interpretation caveat

Null resampling quantifies empirical selection under a globally null DGP. It does not validate FDP control in partly non-null observational data, and label permutation is not a substitute for modeled confounders.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 8), 60, 8,
            dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:60), paste0("f", 1:8)))
y <- setNames(x[, 1] * 2 + rnorm(60), rownames(x))
nv <- stabl_null_check(
  x, y,
  design = "independent",
  fit_spec = list(n_bootstraps = 10,
                  artificial_type = "random_permutation"),
  n_reps = 3, seed = 7
)
nv$p_any_selection
#> [1] 0
